best_for: Students and teachers with a pen tablet who handwrite notes or mark up lecture PDFs on a laptop, and want a free tool with no account.
description:
Xournal++ is a handwriting and note-taking app from the volunteer Xournal++ Team. It is written in C++ as a modern rewrite of the older Xournal program, and parts such as its stroke recognizer still build on Xournal's code.

You pick a paper background for each page, lined for notes, blank for scratch work or plain white for a whiteboard, and you can save your own page templates. A set square and a compass help you draw straight lines and arcs, and shapes can be filled, resized and rotated. A sidebar shows page previews you can reorder. The toolbar can be rearranged, with separate layouts for portrait and landscape, and auto-save and backups guard against a crash. The interface comes in more than 20 languages.

points.title: Made for a stylus
points.text: It reads pen pressure from Wacom, Huion and XP-Pen tablets, smooths shaky lines, and lets you map tools or colors to pen and mouse buttons. Layers, shapes and grid snapping help keep diagrams neat.

points.title: Write on top of PDFs
points.text: You can annotate a PDF, highlight or strike through its text and follow its links. The PDF is not embedded in your `.xopp` file, so moving or deleting the PDF loses the background. Export to PDF, PNG or SVG when you are done.

points.title: Math and recorded lectures
points.text: A LaTeX editor drops formulas into the page, but it needs a working LaTeX install on your machine. You can also record audio while you write and play it back from any stroke.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: It is GPL-2.0 software with no price and no sign-in. Lua plugins let you add your own tools.

points.title: macOS takes extra steps
points.text: The project says the Mac app will not open as released until you run `xattr` and `codesign` commands in Terminal. Homebrew disabled its cask for failing Apple's Gatekeeper check. Separate Intel and Apple silicon downloads exist.

points.title: Windows: user or machine, x64 or Arm
points.text: Windows installers come per-user or machine-wide, for x64 and Arm64, though the README says Windows on Arm is not officially supported. The Windows listing keeps 20 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.

points.title: Linux via a verified Flatpak
points.text: The Flathub build is verified for the Xournal++ team, for x64 and Arm64. For LaTeX inside the Flatpak you also need the TeX Live extension.
